paper.title: The link between physician motivation and care
paper.journal: The European Journal of Health Economics
paper.code_data_availability: Data availablity: “The data used in this study is from pseudoanonymised survey and register data held on a secure server by Statistics Denmark. …

registers.name_in_paper: a nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019
registers.role: treatment (the three measures of work motivation: EM, UO, PSM)
variables_mentioned: validated motivation items measured on a 5-point Likert scale (listed in Online resource 1)
practices’ area of location (region and postal code)

registers.role: sample frame, outcomes (list size per GP, list closure) and controls
variables_mentioned: whether practices are open for uptake of patients

registers.role: outcomes / controls (Charlson Comorbidity Index of enlisted patients)
variables_mentioned: registered diagnoses (ICD10-codes) for patients at Danish hospitals

registers.role: outcomes / controls (eight measures of patients’ socioeconomic status), residence, and degree of urbanisation
variables_mentioned: whether patients live in Denmark in a given period

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish Register of Causes of Death
registers.role: sample frame (whether patients are alive in a given period)

registers.name_in_paper: The Danish National Health Service Register
registers.role: outcomes (FFS per enlisted patient, number of face-to-face consultations per enlisted patient)
variables_mentioned: number of face-to-face consultations performed during regular working hours in 2019

registers.role: outcomes (costs of redeemed prescriptions, number of antibiotic prescriptions, share of narrow-spectrum penicillin)
variables_mentioned: costs of redeemed prescriptions at community pharmacies

linkages: GPs’ survey responses on motivation are linked to administrative register data on their practice’s care; motivation is averaged across the GPs within a practice because care is measured at practice level

Patients are linked to the practice they are enlisted with (the Danish Provider Register), and patient-level health, socioeconomic, fee and prescription records are aggregated to the practice’s enlisted population
Prescriptions are linked to the issuing GP (prescriber) in the Danish National Prescription Register

sample.universe: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (in 2019 there were 3365 registered GPs working in 1720 practices in Denmark)
selection_rules: Practices active the entire year of 2019: practices with a closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019 are defined as inactive and excluded
At least one GP in the practice responded to the motivational survey
Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is included
sample.n_individuals: average number of GPs per practice 2.48; around 69% of sample practices are partnership practices, of which around 44% have responses from more than one GP

construction_notes: Motivation: simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items for each of EM, UO and PSM; ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%, UO = 0.5%, PSM = 3.4%); sum score rescaled min–max to 0–1 so that 0 is the least and 1 the most motivated; averaged across the GPs in a practice who responded.
Confirmatory factor analyses support the EM/UO/PSM dimensions; Cronbach’s alpha is 0.78–0.79 for EM and PSM and 0.48 for UO (three items). All items are kept in the main analysis.
Within-practice variation (average standard deviation) across responding GPs is EM = 0.17, UO = 0.12, PSM = 0.12.

Charlson Comorbidity Index computed from all registered diagnoses (ICD10-codes) for patients at Danish hospitals from 2015 to 2019; because only hospital diagnoses are available this is a lower bound of patients’ health status.
Antibiotics are identified by the ATC-codes J01 and P01AB0; narrow-spectrum penicillin by ATC-code J01CE.
Costs are calculated in Danish kroner, where 1 DKK = 0.13 EUR.
The eight socioeconomic measures of high need take inspiration from the Danish Deprivation Index and are generated from Statistics Denmark’s registers.
FFS and face-to-face consultations refer to services provided during regular working hours in 2019 and are expressed per enlisted patient; DKK 143 is the fee per face-to-face consultation.
Degree of urbanisation follows Statistics Denmark’s DEGURBA definition, based on population density and the number of inhabitants in the largest city in the area.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher EM (financial motivation) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is not statistically significantly associated with Share of enlisted patients who are/have 20–59 year olds and unemployed for at least 6 months, with the other two motivation measures entered in the same regression and no further controls.

treatment.label: EM (extrinsic motivation): the practice’s average degree of financial motivation

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on remuneration, γ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Share of enlisted patients who are/have 20–59 year olds and unemployed for at least 6 months

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark’s registers (variable names not given)

definition.value: One of ten indicators of high-need patients; the share of the practice’s enlisted patients in 2019 who fall in the stated category. The socioeconomic indicators take inspiration from the Danish Deprivation Index and are generated from Statistics Denmark’s registers.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: share of enlisted patients (proportion, 0–1) per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score, i.e. going from the least to the most motivated practice

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted common cause of practice motivation and care; the authors concede that structural factors affecting access to and collaborations with other providers may affect both, so they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

implies_edges.from: Structural factors impacting access to and collaborations with other providers
implies_edges.to: EM (extrinsic motivation): the practice’s average degree of financial motivation

implies_edges.from: Structural factors impacting access to and collaborations with other providers
implies_edges.to: Share of enlisted patients who are/have 20–59 year olds and unemployed for at least 6 months

key_assumptions.assumption: No reverse causality: care does not feed back into practice motivation. The authors state they cannot rule this out (e.g. physicians providing care to many high-need patients may over time become more patient-altruistic).

implies_edges.from: Share of enlisted patients who are/have 20–59 year olds and unemployed for at least 6 months
implies_edges.to: EM (extrinsic motivation): the practice’s average degree of financial motivation

key_assumptions.assumption: The sample is conditioned on at least one GP in the practice having responded to the motivational survey, and the responding practices differ from the study population on observable characteristics and outcomes.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A comparison of the sample with the study population (Online resource 3) and robustness to controlling for degree of urbanisation and region.

implies_edges.from: At least one GP in the practice responded to the motivational survey
implies_edges.to: Inclusion in the estimation sample

key_assumptions.assumption: The practice-level average of the survey scores of the responding GPs measures the motivation of the practice that produces the care; the paper notes this is more precisely measured for single-handed than for partnership practices.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A robustness check restricted to single-handed practices, where the link between GP and practice is direct (Online resource 9); signs and sizes of key estimates are similar.

key_assumptions.assumption: The survey-based motivation scores (EM, UO, PSM) proxy the theoretical relative preference weights γ, α and δ in the physician utility function.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Confirmatory factor analyses showing that the majority of items reflect the dimensions of EM, UO and PSM (Online resource 2); Cronbach’s alpha 0.78–0.79 for EM and PSM, 0.48 for UO.

threats_discussed: Confounding by structural factors impacting access to and collaborations with other providers, which may affect both practice motivation and care
Reversed causality: physicians providing care to many high-need patients may over time become more patient-altruistic
Care can only be measured at the practice level while motivation is measured for individual GPs
The sample differs from the study population on share of single-handed practices, degree of urbanisation and region
Administrative registers capture (apart from prescribing) only services linked with a fee
Diagnoses are available only from hospital registrations, so the Charlson index is a lower bound of patients’ health status
Multicollinearity between the three motivation measures (checked with VIF scores)
robustness_checks: Alternative motivation measures: confirmatory-factor-analysis weighted sum scores; excluding ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses; dichotomised measures at the 50th and 75th percentile of the motivation score distribution (Online resource 5–8)
Restricting the analysis to single-handed practices, where the GP-practice link is direct (Online resource 9)
Controlling for observable structural factors: degree of urbanisation and region of location (Online resource 10)
Adding interaction terms between the motivational components (only 2 of 96 interaction terms statistically significant)
Variance inflation factors (VIF scores) to check multicollinearity
unresolved_confounders: Structural factors impacting access to and collaborations with other providers, which may affect both practice motivation and care
Reversed causality between motivation and care
GP characteristics associated with UO such as GPs’ socioeconomic background and place of birth, which the authors do not have access to

heterogeneity.finding: Restricting the analysis to single-handed practices, where motivation and care are linked directly, leaves the signs and size of the key estimates similar, but statistical significance in some cases drops due to the smaller sample size.

heterogeneity.dimension: how motivation is measured (continuous vs dichotomised at the 50th/75th percentile)
heterogeneity.finding: Dichotomising the motivation scores changes the statistical significance of a few findings (for example the association between PSM and medication costs) but not the sign of the estimates.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher PSM (altruism towards society) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is not statistically significantly associated with Share of enlisted patients who are/have 25–59 year olds without vocational education, with the other two motivation measures entered in the same regression and no further controls.

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ public-service-motivation (altruism towards society) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (PSM = 3.4%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across responding GPs in the practice. definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. register_source.value: The Danish National Patient Register (ICD10 diagnosis codes 2015–2019; variable names not given)

definition.value: One of ten indicators of high-need patients; the share of the practice’s enlisted patients in 2019 with the stated Charlson Comorbidity Index score. The index is computed from all registered diagnoses (ICD10-codes) for patients at Danish hospitals from 2015 to 2019; because diagnoses are only available from hospital registrations it is a lower bound of patients’ health status.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: share of enlisted patients (proportion, 0–1) per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score, i.e. going from the least to the most motivated practice

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher EM (financial motivation) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is associated with a higher value of List size per GP in the practice, with the other two motivation measures entered in the same regression and no further controls.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher UO (altruism towards the patient) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is not statistically significantly associated with Whether the practice operate with a closed list, controlling for who the practices serve and for the other two motivation measures.

treatment.label: UO (user orientation): the practice’s average degree of altruism towards the patient

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ user-orientation (altruism towards the patient) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items (three items, Cronbach’s alpha 0.48), with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (UO = 0.5%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across responding GPs in the practice. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on patient benefits, α.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Whether the practice operate with a closed list

register_source.value: The Danish Provider Register (variable names not given)

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if the practice operates with a closed list, i.e. does not enrol new patients (practices with more than 1,600 patients on their list per GP may close for further uptake); almost two-thirds of the practices operate with a closed list at the start of 2019.

timing.value: Measured at the start of 2019; the care outcomes refer to the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey.

units.value: odds ratio for operating with a closed list, per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score, i.e. going from the least to the most motivated practice

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted common cause of practice motivation and care; the authors concede that structural factors affecting access to and collaborations with other providers may affect both, so they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

links.pointer_quote: Our findings show that practices with higher EM generate more FFS per patient.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher EM (financial motivation) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is associated with a higher value of FFS per enlisted patient (DKK), with the other two motivation measures entered in the same regression and no further controls.

treatment.label: EM (extrinsic motivation): the practice’s average degree of financial motivation

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on remuneration, γ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: FFS per enlisted patient (DKK)

register_source.value: The Danish National Health Service Register (variable names not given)

definition.value: The practice’s total revenue from fee-for-services generated during regular working hours in 2019, divided by its number of enlisted patients, in DKK (1 DKK = 0.13 EUR).

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: DKK of fee-for-services per enlisted patient per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

magnitude.interpretation: A change from the least to the most extrinsically motivated practice is associated with an increase in FFS per patient of 68–88 DKK (8–10% of the mean).

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted common cause of practice motivation and care; the authors concede that structural factors affecting access to and collaborations with other providers may affect both, so they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher EM (financial motivation) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is associated with a higher value of FFS per enlisted patient (DKK), controlling for who and how many patients the practices serve and for the other two motivation measures.

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. units.value: DKK of fee-for-services per enlisted patient per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher PSM (altruism towards society) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is not statistically significantly associated with FFS per enlisted patient (DKK), controlling for who and how many patients the practices serve and for the other two motivation measures.

treatment.label: PSM (public service motivation): the practice’s average degree of altruism towards society

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ public-service-motivation (altruism towards society) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (PSM = 3.4%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across responding GPs in the practice. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on net societal benefits, δ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: FFS per enlisted patient (DKK)

register_source.value: The Danish National Health Service Register (variable names not given)

definition.value: The practice’s total revenue from fee-for-services generated during regular working hours in 2019, divided by its number of enlisted patients, in DKK (1 DKK = 0.13 EUR).

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: DKK of fee-for-services per enlisted patient per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted common cause of practice motivation and care; the authors concede that structural factors affecting access to and collaborations with other providers may affect both, so they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher EM (financial motivation) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is not statistically significantly associated with Costs of all prescriptions redeemed per enlisted patient (DKK), with the other two motivation measures entered in the same regression and no further controls.

treatment.label: EM (extrinsic motivation): the practice’s average degree of financial motivation

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on remuneration, γ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Costs of all prescriptions redeemed per enlisted patient (DKK)

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Register (ATC codes; variable names not given)

definition.value: Total costs of all prescriptions redeemed by the practice’s enlisted patients at community pharmacies in 2019, divided by its number of enlisted patients, in DKK.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: DKK of redeemed prescriptions per enlisted patient per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted common cause of practice motivation and care; the authors concede that structural factors affecting access to and collaborations with other providers may affect both, so they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher PSM (altruism towards society) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is associated with a lower value of Costs of all prescriptions redeemed per enlisted patient (DKK), controlling for who and how many patients the practices serve and for the other two motivation measures.

treatment.label: PSM (public service motivation): the practice’s average degree of altruism towards society

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ public-service-motivation (altruism towards society) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (PSM = 3.4%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across responding GPs in the practice. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on net societal benefits, δ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Costs of all prescriptions redeemed per enlisted patient (DKK)

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Register (ATC codes; variable names not given)

definition.value: Total costs of all prescriptions redeemed by the practice’s enlisted patients at community pharmacies in 2019, divided by its number of enlisted patients, in DKK.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: DKK of redeemed prescriptions per enlisted patient per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

magnitude.interpretation: Going from being the least to the most altruistic towards society is associated with a decrease in medication costs per patient of 145 DKK (10% of the mean).

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher UO (altruism towards the patient) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is associated with a higher value of Number of antibiotic prescriptions issued by the GP per enlisted patient, controlling for who and how many patients the practices serve and for the other two motivation measures.

treatment.label: UO (user orientation): the practice’s average degree of altruism towards the patient

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ user-orientation (altruism towards the patient) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items (three items, Cronbach’s alpha 0.48), with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (UO = 0.5%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across responding GPs in the practice. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on patient benefits, α.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Number of antibiotic prescriptions issued by the GP per enlisted patient

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Register (ATC codes; variable names not given)

definition.value: Number of redeemed antibiotic prescriptions issued by the GP per enlisted patient in 2019; antibiotics are identified by the ATC-codes J01 and P01AB0.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: antibiotic prescriptions per enlisted patient per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

magnitude.interpretation: UO is associated with issuing 0.03–0.07 more prescriptions of antibiotics per patient (12–26% of the mean)

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher EM (financial motivation) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is not statistically significantly associated with Share of narrow-spectrum penicillin issued by the GP to enlisted patients, with the other two motivation measures entered in the same regression and no further controls.

treatment.label: EM (extrinsic motivation): the practice’s average degree of financial motivation

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ extrinsic-motivation (financial motives) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated items measured on a 5-point Likert scale, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (EM = 1.2%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across the GPs in the practice who responded to the survey. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on remuneration, γ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Share of narrow-spectrum penicillin issued by the GP to enlisted patients

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Register (ATC codes; variable names not given)

definition.value: Share of the antibiotics issued by the GP to enlisted patients in 2019 that is narrow-spectrum penicillin (ATC-code J01CE); a quality measure related to the clinical guidelines, since narrow-spectrum penicillin reduces the risk of antimicrobial resistance.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: share of antibiotics that is narrow-spectrum penicillin (proportion, 0–1) per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

estimand.target_population: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 with at least one GP responding to the 2019 motivational survey
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: motivation measured in the 2019 survey, care measured over the calendar year 2019; no dynamic horizon is estimated.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

population.description: Danish general practices active the entire year of 2019 (no closing date registered in the Provider Register during 2019) with at least one GP responding to the nation-wide motivational survey; 795 practices, 50% of the study population. Only care given to patients who live in Denmark and do not die during a given month in 2019 is counted.
population.selection: Practices are in the sample only if at least one of their GPs responded to the nation-wide motivational survey; the sample is less often single-handed, has slightly fewer low-socioeconomic-status patients, 59 fewer patients on the list on average, DKK 27 higher FFS per patient, and is more rural than the study population.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported work motivation across Danish general practices in 2019; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used, and the authors state they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted common cause of practice motivation and care; the authors concede that structural factors affecting access to and collaborations with other providers may affect both, so they cannot provide unequivocal evidence of a causal relationship.
key_assumptions.supported_by: A supplementary analysis controlling for the practices’ region and degree of urbanisation, which are related to such structural factors (Online resource 10); VIF scores are calculated to check multicollinearity.

claims.statement: In Danish general practice in 2019, a one-unit higher PSM (altruism towards society) score (going from the least to the most motivated practice) is associated with a higher value of Share of narrow-spectrum penicillin issued by the GP to enlisted patients, controlling for who and how many patients the practices serve and for the other two motivation measures.

treatment.label: PSM (public service motivation): the practice’s average degree of altruism towards society

register_source.value: Nation-wide survey of Danish GPs from 2019 (survey data linked to Statistics Denmark registers; the paper names no register variable for motivation)

definition.value: Practice-level average of GPs’ public-service-motivation (altruism towards society) score: a simple sum score of the GP’s responses to validated 5-point Likert items, with ‘do not know/not relevant’ responses mean-imputed (PSM = 3.4%), rescaled min–max to 0–1 (0 = least motivated, 1 = most motivated), then averaged across responding GPs in the practice. Used as an empirical proxy for the relative preference weight on net societal benefits, δ.

timing.value: Measured in the nation-wide survey of Danish GPs fielded in 2019; aggregated to the practice as the average over the GPs in the practice who responded. Contemporaneous with the 2019 care outcomes (single cross-section).

outcome.label: Share of narrow-spectrum penicillin issued by the GP to enlisted patients

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Register (ATC codes; variable names not given)

definition.value: Share of the antibiotics issued by the GP to enlisted patients in 2019 that is narrow-spectrum penicillin (ATC-code J01CE); a quality measure related to the clinical guidelines, since narrow-spectrum penicillin reduces the risk of antimicrobial resistance.

timing.value: Measured over the calendar year 2019, contemporaneous with the 2019 motivation survey (single cross-section).

units.value: share of antibiotics that is narrow-spectrum penicillin (proportion, 0–1) per one-unit increase in the 0–1 motivation score

magnitude.interpretation: Going from being the least to the most altruistic towards society increases the share of prescribed narrow-spectrum penicillin by 3.3 percentage points (12% of the mean) when taking into account who and how many patients that are served.
